This is a hugely promising Globe debut from Lown-Collins, brimming with imagination and really evoking the soul of flamenco through Shakespeare.
This is a charming, intelligent evening of theatre that proves Shakespeare does not always need reinvention.
Not everything works but it makes for an enjoyable Iberian minibreak on Bankside and leaves you feeling that it might be fun to try a flamenco class.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this flamenco-infused production, with some praising its creative energy and Spanish heat, while others find it fails to overcome the play's challenging material and flimsy structure.
